subject: Inference SLA & burn-rate plan for Tempo Retail
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@tempo-retail.com>, Tim Cho <tim.cho@tempo-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery + initial perf targets / proposed next steps

Hi Anna / Tim — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we’re all aligned. I attached a preliminary cost model and a short benchmarking plan for reference.

High-level product goals you emphasized:
- Low-latency chat for customers with streaming partial responses to UI (important for perceived responsiveness)
- Support high-concurrency storefront queries during peak hours (holiday campaigns)
- Predictable per-call SLOs so ops can route traffic and alert on regressions

Initial perf targets (from today's discovery):
- P95 generation latency target: 150ms for 1–2 sentence responses (you mentioned 200ms target; we outlined a more aggressive baseline during the call)
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec with spikes to 500 req/sec for short windows
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent user sessions with streaming token-by-token experience
- Streaming requirement: server-sent tokens within 40–60ms per token when generating

Cost / performance levers we discussed to hit the SLOs:
- Continuous batching to increase GPU utilization without blowing P95s
- Prefix (prompt) caching for repeat/templated prompts during campaign bursts
- Quantization profile options (4-bit & 8-bit) for model variants to trade quality <-> cost
- Model variants / fallbacks (full 13B for peak quality, 7B-quant for low-cost baseline with identical interface)

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Technical deep dive with Dylan (infra) to validate streaming requirements + run sample perf tests (60–90 minute session) — propose Tue 26 May or Wed 27 May, let us know preferred slot.
2) Redwood to deliver two burn-rate scenarios by EOD Mon 25 May: hosted (burstable) vs. dedicated capacity (reserved) with expected per-1M token cost and margin impact.
3) Tempo to share a short traffic shape (15–30 day forecast / peak adjustments) and 3 representative prompts for caching tests.

Attachments: redwood-prelim-cost-model.xlsx (prelim cost scenarios), latency-benchmarking-plan.md (test plan / sample prompts).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the deep dive and loop in engineering.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Anna Lee <anna@tempo-retail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@tempo-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + initial perf targets / proposed next steps

Thanks Karthik — this is great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming is non-negotiable for our UX — we need token-level partials in the web chat client for perceived latency. 40ms per token would be ideal; we can tolerate up to 80ms on slow networks.
- P95 target: our internal bar is 200ms for short outputs, but if you can show consistent 150ms we'd be open to that as a stretch SLA.
- Concurrency expectation: 50 concurrent live chats during normal peaks, but one of our promos last year saw short bursts up to 300 concurrent. We don't expect sustained 300, but it happened for ~3–5 minutes.

We’ll attach the 30-day traffic shape and 3 sample prompts (coming in a follow-up email). For the TD, Wed 27 May afternoon (US/PST) works best for our infra and product leads.

Two questions to flag so Dylan can prep:
1) Can you support partial streaming while also applying prefix caching? Any tradeoffs we should know about?
2) For the quantized model variants, do you have internal numbers on quality delta (BLEU/ARO-like metrics) vs. unquantized baseline, or will we need an eval run?

Appreciate it — will share artifacts in the follow-up.

Best,
Anna
Head of Product | Tempo Retail
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@tempo-retail.com>, Tim Cho <tim.cho@tempo-retail.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + initial perf targets / proposed next steps

Thanks Anna — perfect. Answers up front so Dylan can prepare for Wed 27:00 PDT deep dive.

1) Streaming + prefix caching: supported. Tradeoffs: caching reduces token-generation work when the same prompt prefixes recur, but for token-level streaming we prioritize low-latency emit paths — caching is applied to KV cache / prefix embeddings and then we schedule the remaining generation into small continuous batches. In practice, we see ~30–45% cost reduction for templated prompts with negligible impact to first-token latency, but you should expect some variance for long-tail prompts.

2) Quantization quality delta: we have internal evals comparing 7B & 13B float baselines to 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants. Typical differences: 8-bit almost indistinguishable on short conversational replies; 4-bit shows minor degradations on rare edge-cases (long-chain reasoning) but is usually acceptable for templated responses. We’ll bring per-metric snapshots to the TD; if you prefer we can run your prompt set against 4- and 8-bit variants during the pilot.

Proposed TD agenda (60–90 min):
- Confirm exact streaming semantics and token flush timings you need
- Share sample traffic/traffic shape and run-through of latency-benchmarking-plan.md
- Run a short on-the-spot perf run with 7B-quant vs 13B baseline (synthetic) to show delta
- Discuss capacity / pricing (hosted burst vs dedicated reserved) and operational fallbacks for brief spikes

I’ll schedule Wed 27 May 14:00–15:30 PDT and invite Dylan + Marissa. If that slot is bad, tell me and we’ll move.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Prep for Tempo TD (Wed 27) + deliverables

Marissa / Dylan — thread above with Tempo. Wed 27 May 14:00–15:30 PDT confirmed as the technical deep dive. Action items: 

Dylan:
- Run two quick synthetic benchmarks (by Tue EOD 26 May) using our infra: 7B-quant (4-bit) and 13B-fp16 baseline. Collect P50/P95 token latencies, end-to-end P95 for 1–2 sentence outputs, and per-token emit latency under continuous batching. Save results to the shared drive link in related_links.
- Prepare a short slide with caching behavior notes (expected hit rates for templated prompts, estimated cost reduction %)

Marissa:
- Finalize and sanity-check the draft hosted vs reserved burn-rate scenarios in redwood-prelim-cost-model.xlsx and add a 'probable commercial ask' note showing committed monthly spend tiers that would move Tempo to Dedicated. Target: EOD Mon 25 May.

Karthik (me) will:
- Update the TD agenda with Tempo's streaming tolerances (40–80ms) and the high-burst window (300 concurrent for ~3–5 min).
- Request Tempo’s 30-day traffic shape and sample prompts (Anna said she’ll send).

Keep this tight — Tempo is schedule-sensitive. If you run into infra constraints for on-the-spot runs, prepare a recorded perf run we can share during the call.

Thanks — let’s sync briefly Mon morning if there are any blockers.

Karthik
--- End of thread ---
